extracted.intended_audience: researchers, librarians, journal editors, and citation-management software developers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for how researchers, journals, and citation tools should handle citations to retracted articles (e.g., explicitly documenting retractions, citation-style rules, and software flagging). Focus is on scholarly citation practice and communication around retracted literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retracted status in citations
rubrics_metrics.description: "My team felt that documenting the retraction carries a great amount of weight in demonstrating that the findings were fraudulent..." — explicitly note when a cited paper has been retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, indicate in the citation or text that the work has been retracted (so readers understand the findings are not valid). The interview notes that many authors used terms like "flawed" or "false" but still did not document the retracted status; documenting the retraction is less open to interpretation than subjective descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require 'Retraction:' label in citation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: "At the bare-minimum, guidelines should require the word 'Retraction:' to appear before the article title of a retracted article."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation style manuals and journal instructions should mandate a standardized, prominent label (e.g., leading 'Retraction:') in the bibliographic entry so the retracted status is unambiguous and visible in automatically generated bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation styles should include retraction guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all citation styles provide guidelines for citing retractions; AMA explicitly states how, APA gives web guidance but not in their manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style manuals should incorporate explicit instructions on how to cite retracted articles (in the manual, not only on websites) to ensure consistent practice across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals should hold authors accountable for reference accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "...journals need to hold authors accountable for ensuring that their references are accurate." Journals currently vary in whether they check reference accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While checking every reference is complicated, journals should establish policies and processes that require authors to verify references (including retraction status) and should consider spot-checking or automated checking to reduce citation of problematic literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation managers should automatically flag and update retracted items
rubrics_metrics.description: "Zotero ... now includes an enhancement that will identify retracted articles that have been downloaded into a Zotero library" and recommendation that "All citation managers should seriously consider this functionality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation-management software (e.g., Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote) should implement automatic detection and library-wide updates for retracted articles so users are notified and bibliographies reflect retraction status without manual checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must verify imported references and not rely blindly on managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Many authors are overly reliant on citation managers; import can bury 'retracted' notices so automatically generated bibliography entries may omit retraction information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After importing citations, authors should verify bibliographic entries (including retraction flags) and confirm the current status of items in their libraries, especially before submission/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure bibliographies display retraction notices prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'retracted' notice is often buried when citation information is imported and does not show up in automatically generated bibliography entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliography formatting and citation-generator tools should ensure that retraction labels are included and visible in the final reference list (e.g., by prepending 'Retraction:' or adding a clear retraction note in the entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific retraction notices/versions (partial vs full)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors were surprised that few referenced the 2004 partial retraction because partial retractions are unusual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paper has undergone partial retraction or other post-publication updates, cite the specific retraction notice/version and make clear which parts were retracted or corrected so readers understand the exact status of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware that negative/negational citations still increase visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Even negative citations (negational references) count toward citation metrics and can increase an article's ranking in databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and evaluators should recognize that any citation—affirmative or negative—boosts citation counts; databases and evaluative frameworks may need to account for citation context to avoid unintentionally amplifying retracted or fraudulent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewers and editors should check references for accuracy and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters reported that referees often read reference lists and notice errors (misspellings, incorrect names) and sometimes spot issues authors missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of peer review and editorial oversight, reviewers and editors should inspect reference lists for basic accuracy and question citations to problematic or outdated literature, including checking for subsequent retractions of works cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researchers should periodically re-check previously collected literature for retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may have an older 'pre-retraction' copy of an article that was subsequently retracted and may not realize the article was later retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain periodic checks of items in personal and lab citation libraries (or rely on software that does so) to ensure previously collected literature hasn't been retracted since it was first read or imported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate research clearly to public to reduce misinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: For those unfamiliar with the research (students, other disciplines, public), the number of citations a retracted study receives can be misleading; scientists need to make findings easier to understand and emphasize relevance to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should improve public-facing communication of research findings (clarity, relevance, shareability) to help prevent misinterpretation of scholarly citation counts and to counter misleading amplification of retracted work on social media.
